description: 🚀 Orbit of D. is a team driven by curiosity, creativity, and the spirit of exploration. Inspired by NASA's discoveries and One Piece's unbreakable will to explore the unknown, we're taking on NASA Space Apps 2026's “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge. Our goal is to bring the stories of NASA's forgotten equipment on the Moon and Mars to life through an interactive experience. We welcome passionate minds ready to explore beyond limits! 🌌
summary: OFFWORLD LEGACY is an interactive digital archive that tells the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars. It documents six historic missions: Surveyor 3, Apollo 12 ALSEP, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Viking 1, and Opportunity. Visitors can explore each machine's purpose, deployment, scientific contributions, operational timeline, final communications, and known physical disposition. The website combines NASA-sourced historical information, archival imagery, interactive location markers, mission timelines, and student-friendly explanations. By distinguishing equipment shutdown, last communication, mission closure, and physical recovery, OFFWORLD LEGACY helps people understand not only what humanity sent to other worlds, but also what remains of those missions and why their legacy matters.
details:
OFFWORLD LEGACY is an interactive digital museum developed in response to the challenge of storytelling about NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars.

The platform documents six historic equipment records across two planetary destinations: Surveyor 3, Apollo 12 ALSEP, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Viking 1 Lander, and Opportunity Rover.

Users can explore mission stories, search and filter the archive, examine chronological timelines, view documented surface locations, and learn about the scientific instruments and communication systems used during these missions.

The project addresses an important educational problem: information about abandoned planetary equipment is distributed across historical mission records, scientific publications, and image archives. OFFWORLD LEGACY brings this information together in an accessible experience.

A key feature is its evidence-based timeline design, which distinguishes last successful data transmission, final signal, equipment shutdown, subsystem failure, and formal mission closure. Its recovery overview also distinguishes recovered components from equipment whose physical condition is not confirmed.

The application was developed using React, JavaScript, Vite, and responsive CSS. NASA mission histories, technical records, and archival imagery provide its research foundation.

Our goal is to preserve the scientific and historical legacy of planetary exploration and help students and the public understand the human footprint left beyond Earth.
